beachport-6.name: Southend Beach
beachport-6.bio: A sheltered Rivoli Bay beach beside the village of Southend, used for swimming, sailing and boating.

notes.pin: Pin the beach itself (OSM natural=beach on Rivoli Bay at Southend), not the village centre. Parking is free.
notes.text: Draft said beach, boating and a cafe; the cafe is unsourced so dropped. Sailing is from the Rivoli Bay Sailing Club off the beach (southaustralia.com).

beachport-7.name: Millicent Museum
beachport-7.bio: A National Trust museum in an 1873 school building with a shipwreck room and a large horse-drawn vehicle collection.

notes.pin: 1 Mount Gambier Road, Millicent (NT page address); it shares the Visitor Information Centre complex.
notes.text: Renamed from Millicent National Trust Museum: the Trust now titles it 'Millicent Museum'. Adult $14, concession $10, children 5-15 $2 per the NT page (may be dated). Open Mon-Fri 9-5, Sat-Sun and public holidays 10-4. The 'gallery' of the draft is not sourced; the shipwreck room and carriages are.
notes.review: Millicent is about 35 km from Beachport; kept in beachport per draft.

naracoorte-1.name: Naracoorte Caves National Park
naracoorte-1.bio: South Australia's World Heritage fossil caves, with guided tours, a fossil centre and a bat observation centre.
naracoorte-1.coordinates_source: provisional draft (Wikipedia); pending serial pin pass

notes.pin: Wikivoyage geotag -37.035658,140.796569 and Caves Cafe -37.036163,140.7966 mark the Wonambi visitor centre area; use that visitor point.
notes.text: Park entry is free; tours are paid. Adult tours: Stick-Tomato Cave self-guided $13.50 (includes Wonambi Fossil Centre), Wonambi alone $8.50, Alexandra Cave $28.50 (30 min), Bat Tour $33 (1 hr), Victoria Fossil Cave $40.50 (1 hr), 90-minute adventure/World Heritage tours up to $79.50. Range is the main guided/self-guided cave tours. Open 9am-5pm. Bat tours depend on season (bats away in colder months): not verified.

naracoorte-4.name: Coonawarra

notes.pin: Pin on the cellar-door strip along the Riddoch Highway at Coonawarra locality (e.g. OSM place=locality/hamlet Coonawarra), not Penola town.
notes.text: Category left as drafted ('nature') since the schema has no wine category; consider 'historic'/'nature' at review. Free as a region; cellar-door tastings are individually priced (not stored).

notes.pin: The 500 m boardwalk is at the Bool Lagoon main visitor area (Little Bool Lagoon side); Gahnia Walk (430 m return) starts at the main entrance car park. Use the boardwalk/entrance car park, not the reserve centroid.

destination.name: Naracoorte
destination.tagline: A farming town beside South Australia's fossil caves and the Coonawarra's red-soil vineyards.
destination.description: Naracoorte is a Limestone Coast town on the road between Adelaide and Melbourne. South of town, Naracoorte Caves National Park is South Australia's only World Heritage site, with caves that preserved the bones of Australian megafauna over the last two to three million years. To the south the terra rossa soil of Coonawarra and Penola grows Cabernet Sauvignon, while Bool Lagoon to the south-west is a large wetland for waterbirds. The town's flour-mill museum covers the wool industry.

goodToKnow.title: Cave entry is free
goodToKnow.detail: Entering Naracoorte Caves National Park costs nothing, but every cave tour is ticketed, so book ahead online for the longer ones.

goodToKnow.title: Bat season varies
goodToKnow.detail: Bats use the Bat Centre cave only part of the year, so check the park's bat information before planning around the evening flight.

goodToKnow.title: Cellar doors on one road
goodToKnow.detail: More than 20 Coonawarra cellar doors sit along a single stretch of road, so they are easy to link in a half day.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring mild days for cave tours, cellar doors and wetland walks.
